column1: # SYNTHETIC drug catalogue for the demo case. Every agent is FICTIONAL.
# The catalogue deliberately mirrors the real failure mode it must defeat: agents that
# bind the correct target but push it in the WRONG direction score highly on any naive
# target-proximity search, because a checkpoint-deficiency disease and a checkpoint-
# inhibitor oncology programme share the same pathway vocabulary. Direction is signed
# here so the pipeline can reject them (GP-16).

column8: Binds and stabilises the assembled synthetic mitotic checkpoint complex, prolonging its inhibitory signal and partially compensating for reduced SynthKin1 abundance.
column21: Quantify missegregation rate and micronucleus frequency in patient-derived fibroblasts across a clinically achievable dose range, with an isogenic corrected control and a blinded scorer.
column22: Right target, right direction, in vivo evidence, paediatric exposure. Expected top-ranked candidate.

column8: Potent ATP-competitive inhibitor of the synthetic checkpoint kinase. Abrogates checkpoint signalling, causing premature mitotic exit and marked aneuploidy. Developed to push chromosomally unstable tumour cells past their aneuploidy-tolerance ceiling.
column21: None. This agent must not be advanced; it moves the target in the disease direction.
column22: WRONG DIRECTION. Surfaces at the top of any target-proximity search because it binds the exact pathway named in the mechanism. Must be rejected.

column8: Chemical probe that stabilises the synthetic checkpoint complex in vitro. Never administered to humans.
column21: Establish an in vivo formulation and measure exposure before any efficacy claim; currently only a binding-assay result exists.
column22: Right direction but NOT approved. Not a repurposing candidate; must be classified as such rather than ranked alongside approved agents.

column8: Positive allosteric modulator used for seizure control. Acts on the organismal phenotype, not on the checkpoint mechanism.
column21: Not applicable as mechanism correction. Standard seizure-management evaluation only.
column22: SYMPTOM MANAGEMENT, not mechanism correction. Must never be presented as disease-modifying.

column8: Alters synthetic microtubule dynamics. Published effects on missegregation are bidirectional: reduces it in some contexts and increases it in others, depending on dose and baseline instability mechanism.
column21: Dose-response missegregation assay in the patient's own cell background to establish the sign of the effect before any further consideration.
column22: CONTEXT_DEPENDENT direction. Must resolve to "cannot determine agreement" -- never counted as agreement, never rejected as wrong-direction.

column8: Inhibits a transporter unrelated to the checkpoint mechanism.
column21: Not applicable; the target is not part of the mechanism chain.
column22: Target is NOT in the mechanism. Must be rejected as TARGET_NOT_IN_MECHANISM rather than scored.

column8: Modulates synthetic microtubule dynamics. Published effects on missegregation are bidirectional and depend on dose and baseline instability mechanism, so no single sign can be assigned. Unlike Synthaxel, its effect on chromosomal instability HAS been characterised and is neutral.
column21: Dose-response missegregation assay in the patient's own cell background to establish the SIGN of the effect. The magnitude question is open; the chromosomal-instability question is already answered.
column22: CONTEXT_DEPENDENT direction with an ASSESSED CIN risk. Must resolve to 'cannot determine agreement' and remain ACCEPTED -- never counted as agreement, never rejected as wrong-direction, and not rejected for oncogenic risk because the risk was measured. Carries the ASSUMPTION-DRUG-02 lesson that SYNTH-DRUG-E used to carry (see ADR 0011).
